ahb_security_features.name: HPROT[1] Privileged
ahb_security_features.purpose: Indicates Unprivileged vs Privileged operating level for an access. Allows Subordinates to enforce privilege checks at the bus layer.

ahb_security_features.name: HNONSEC (AHB5)
ahb_security_features.purpose: Indicates Secure (0) vs Non-secure (1) transfer. Supported only if AHB5 Secure_Transfers property True. Must be constant throughout a burst. Address-phase signal.

ahb_security_features.name: HEXCL + HMASTER + HEXOKAY (AHB5)
ahb_security_features.purpose: Exclusive Access mechanism for safe shared-resource read-modify-write (semaphores, locks); does not by itself provide confidentiality but supports concurrency-safe primitives.

ahb_security_features.name: HMASTLOCK
ahb_security_features.purpose: Locked-sequence indicator — bus is indivisible during a locked sequence; useful for legacy SWP-like atomic operations (multi-Manager configurations).

ahb_security_features.name: AHB5 Interface protection using parity (Chapter 12)
ahb_security_features.purpose: Single-bit fault detection on each interface — improves robustness against random faults but is not a cryptographic integrity feature.

apb_security_features.name: PPROT[0] Normal/Privileged (APB4)
apb_security_features.purpose: Used by some Managers to indicate processing mode; privileged mode typically has greater access within a system.

apb_security_features.name: PPROT[1] Secure/Non-secure (APB4)
apb_security_features.purpose: Distinguishes secure vs non-secure access. LOW = secure, HIGH = non-secure (per IHI 0024C Table 3-1). Used for TrustZone-like address-space partitioning.

apb_security_features.name: PPROT[2] Data/Instruction (APB4)
apb_security_features.purpose: Indicates data vs instruction access (hint; not always accurate for mixed transactions).

what_is_NOT_in_the_specs: No confidentiality / encryption at the protocol layer (no AES, no cipher).
No data-integrity / authentication (no MAC, no HMAC, no signature).
secure_integration_responsibilities: TrustZone partitioning: integrator routes HNONSEC / PPROT[1] to Subordinate-side filters; non-secure accesses to secure regions returned as DECERR-equivalent ERROR.
Master Security Wrappers: external IP / interconnect enforces HNONSEC + HMASTER values per port.
PPROT[1] convention: bit value HIGH = Non-secure (asserted-HIGH-for-Non-secure) — integrators must mirror this convention end-to-end.
fields.notes: Security in AMBA AHB and APB is limited to signaling primitives (HPROT / HNONSEC / PPROT / Exclusive Access / Lock + AHB5 parity) — not cryptographic primitives. End-to-end confidentiality/integrity must be provided by upper layers (TrustZone Address Space Controllers, MMU/SMMU, dedicated crypto IP, secure boot ROM). The specs explicitly note that the Data/Instruction bit is provided as a hint and is not accurate in all cases.

evidence.quote: AHB5 defines the Secure_Transfers property. An interface that supports Secure transfers has an additional signal, HNONSEC. This signal is asserted for a Non-secure transfer and deasserted for a Secure transfer. HNONSEC is an address phase signal and must be constant throughout a burst.
Exclusive Access Monitor records (address, HMASTER) for an exclusive read; on exclusive write, monitor consulted to decide HEXOKAY=1 (success) or HEXOKAY=0 (failure).
Parity check signals can be used to provide interface protection for AHB. Single-bit error detection capability.

PPROT[0] 1=privileged access / 0=normal access; PPROT[1] 1=nonsecure access / 0=secure access (this bit is configured so that when it is HIGH then the transaction is considered non-secure); PPROT[2] 1=instruction access / 0=data access. The primary use of PPROT is as an identifier for Secure or Non-secure transactions.
